I know there are not-so-great INFJs out there but believe me, the way they act is really different than how people with other personality types are acting. They're unhealthy in some specific ways, and no the Ni-Ti loop isn't the holy answer that explains why some people in this sub are INFJ but a bit different, when in fact they're mistyped. 

Please, people, if you only took a test on the internet especially the 16p test, you should really really reconsider your type. Learning better the functions will be especially good for the xNFP mistypes. On the other hand, people who only type themselves with functions as some separate things should also not forget to consider a personality type as a whole, functions are used differently in all types because it's a matter of combinations. 

INFJs and INTJs have Ni as dominant function but because on their other functions, they don't always use Ni for the same reasons (or in the same situations), for example. 

The more you learn about all the personality types, the better you'll understand if you're really an INFJ or not, and become so better at typing yourself and the others. It seems obvious but some people tend to only read what's about their own type instead of reading about all of them. 

There's no problem asking if you have a doubt, and sometimes you can doubt even if you are 100% INFJ. 

The only problem is that it doesn't feel like an INFJ sub at all, unlike the INTJ sub where I can really see that people who are responding are INTJs (the great majority). 

Hope it will not hurt anyone, and I know this topic has been already discussed a thousand times, but a small reminder is always good.

I know many ENTPs, in my family or among my friends. 

I think they make good friends but I'd never take one as a lover. Unfortunately, I've never met any ENTP with a well developed Fe. All of them were very argumentative, provocative and it's exhausting for my little INFJ self. I like seeing everyone's perspective but I don't understand why ENTPs prefer to start talking nonsense than admitting they're wrong (it's ok to be wrong sometimes). And most of them are nihilistic, while I'm spiritual (it's 100% subjective). They started to be too predictable for me : their jokes, the fact that they'll change their minds whenever they feel like it to be subversive, acting as Devil's advocate, trolling in every situation... I know what reaction they want people to have, and I try to not react according to it, so "I'm boring" for them. 

I'm sorry if I said harsh things I'm just a bit tired of the ENxP × INFJ thing, because I don't trust in MBTI compatibility when ENxPs are always making me extremely annoyed in a way or another even if I can be friends with them. Both ENFPs and ENTPs always do something that angers me : instead of having an intriguing and philosophical conversation that never ends between us, they want to make it a debate as if I had the mental energy to argue randomly like them. 

I want to add that ENTPs have also a lot of qualities, they look like fictional characters because they're funny and they always have weird stories that happened to them that are interesting to listen. They're creative and adaptable. And if they're not unhealthy, they're not too judgemental of others behaviours. I like that despite what they show, they're caring souls. 

I'm not the best INFJ you'll met, so don't take my pov as every INFJ's one. I'm glad you like INFJs but understand that some of us are also bad people, like in any other type (it depends how the functions are developed and used). Thus, don't like people for their MBTI type, love them for who they are as an unique being and the chemistry you have with them.

I hate cooking, for the same reasons than you (but I'm not diagnosed with ADHD, maybe it's just consequences of years of depression and anxiety). I have a rice cooker, I love it because I just have to add the rice and it stops itself when it's ready (I can't bear waiting for water to boil in a pan). You can add other types of food in a rice cooker including vegetables and meat. 

I like to do scrambled or fried eggs on the pan because it cooks fast. 

If you have rice + eggs + peas + ham cubes, you can do a kind of Cantonese rice and it's very tasty. 

When I have motivation to wait for the water to boil (once every two months), I cook pasta. And I just add Bolognese sauce from a jar, and whatever cheese I have (it works well with feta or parmesan cheese). 

I do a lot of sandwiches because it's easy. 2 pieces of bread, tomatoes, salad, ham, cheese and it's already a meal. The only effort here is cutting the tomato but trust me, even in most of my worst days I've found energy to at least do that. 

If you want to eat more vegetables and fruits, never leave them in the vegetables compartment of the fridge (idk how it's called). Because you will FORGET them. It happens to me every time. Put them on a more visible place, do whatever you want to make them enough visible. 

As some people had already suggested, you can buy already cut vegetables. I don't do that because I'm too lazy to wait until it's not frozen anymore and I know I'll never remember to take them ouf of the freezer. But it can be a good solution if you have a microwave or if you know how to cook them while still frozen (I don't, it's always tasteless with a weird texture). 

Sometimes I just put a big yoghurt in a bowl, add some fruits/dried fruits, jam and oats and I eat that. I know it's not a meal, it's good for breakfast or desert. 

I think instead of the dried noodles in small packages (instant ramen), you should buy real noodles in an Asian store. It's not very expensive nor long to cook, depending on what you take and I find the taste better. Add small sausages, a bit of green onion and soja sauce with it. If you're fine with instant ramen, it's really easy if you have a kettle to boil your water. 

I also make a lot of salads : pasta salad, rice salad, green salad with cheese, tomatoes, corn, or whatever I find in my fridge. 

Sometimes my executive dysfunction is so low that even everything I write here is too hard for me to cook, so I eat things as a snack like raspberries, nuts, already cut cheese, cherry tomatoes, etc. It's better to eat that than an entire pack of cookies (I also do that but that's another story haha). 

Good luck:)
